meta.title: Siaya health indicators by source, vintage and geography
meta.rule: Aggregates only (no individuals, no patient-level data). Every value keeps its own source, page, period, age group and geography. Vintages are never merged; conflicting values are recorded side by side. County press figures are secondary reports. Sentinel-site values are never county-representative.

confidence_scale.5: Primary official table, design-based county estimate with adequate sample
confidence_scale.4: Primary survey table or primary modelled-estimate report
confidence_scale.3: Primary source with a small sample, or a plan quoting a named estimate
confidence_scale.2: Plan or poster figure with unclear denominator, or a value read from a chart label
confidence_scale.1: Secondary report whose original source is not named or not retrievable

definitions.geography: county = whole Siaya County; sub-county = one of the six sub-counties; sentinel-site = a surveillance area inside Siaya, not county-representative
definitions.pdf_page: 1-based page of the PDF file; null for web pages (see page_note)
definitions.status: primary = value read from the issuing body's own publication; secondary report = value quoted by another document; sentinel-site = surveillance-area study

conflicts.note: Eight model vintages, age bands (15-49, 15+, overall, 13-34) and one press figure. NSDCC says vintages are not comparable; do not draw a trend line across them. Inside SCASP-2015 the text on PDF p.16 says 21.4% (2013) and 23.7% (2014), while Table 1 prints 23.7% under 2013. The 9.8% (2023) press figure matches no vintage held.
96% (KHIS, programme uptake, Dec 2021) against 53.7% (NSDCC 2025 cascade, 3rd 95). Denominators differ or are not printed; neither is preferred.

Related: tb-inc-health01. Same plan gives 292/100,000 (MOH 2022) and 310/100,000 (TIBU 2022) for 2022; the May 2026 article gives incidence 363/100,000 with no source. Prevalence and incidence are different measures.
Review chapter says 87% in 2022; the indicator matrix (PDF p.107, printed p.88) gives a baseline of 89% for the proportion cured.
Same plan gives 19% ('MICS') and 29% ('Malaria cluster indicator survey 2022'); the article gives 24%. No age group, test method or survey report is named for any of them.
KDHS 2022 94.9% (survey, births in last 2 years) against CIDP 95% and 93% (routine data, denominator not stated).
KDHS 2022 84.4% against KHIS 98%. Routine data usually divide by expected births and count deliveries by facility location.
CIDP 20.7% is attributed to Nawiri/Stawisha 2019 on one page and to KDHS on another; KDHS gives 24.7% (2014) and 19.2% (2022).
Related: imm-cidp-review. Definitions differ by round (2014 'fully vaccinated' vs 2022 national schedule) and the CIDP 88% covers an undefined target population.
